_label: SYNTHETIC. Hand-written by the eval author (Claude) for benchmark 4; not real visits. Spots are the five Vasai spot types; dates are October 2026.

notes.body: Falling tide at 17:20 and the mudflats opened up fast. Six Little Egrets worked the channel edge and a Western Reef Heron, dark morph, stood apart near the mangroves. Stayed on the bund the whole time; humid, apparent 31°C.
Evening on the terrace. House Crows went to roost over the water tank around 18:20 and the sky was hazy orange, US AQI 118. Two Rose-ringed Parakeets screeched past heading west.
Walked the outer wall of the fort after a short drizzle. A Spotted Owlet called from a hole in the old church facade, possibly two. Moss was bright green on the bastion steps, slippery.
High tide at 16:50 pushed the waterline right up to the casuarinas. A flock of about forty Brown-headed Gulls sat on the sand, facing into a strong westerly wind. Fishing boats were coming in.
Morning loop around the lake in the park. Indian Pond Herons on every lotus patch, and a White-breasted Waterhen crossed the path with two chicks. Joggers everywhere by 07:00.
Pied Kingfisher hovering over the creek mouth, dropping straight down twice. Fairly confident on a Common Kingfisher too, a flash of blue low over the water. Rising tide, light breeze.
Hot and still afternoon inside the fort walls, felt like 36°C. A Shikra sat in the banyan by the gate and every bulbul in the area was scolding it. Didn't stay long, too much glare.
Heavy shower at 15:30, the first proper rain in a week. After it cleared, dozens of swifts fed low over the rooftops, chasing flying ants coming out of the wet ground.
Low tide at dawn exposed the rocky shelf at the north end. Lesser Sand Plovers ran between the pools and a Whimbrel probed under the seaweed. Watched the tide turn from the dry sand.
A Coppersmith Barbet tuk-tuk-tuked from the fig tree near the children's play area all morning. Quiet otherwise; overcast and cool after the night's rain.
Spring tide, very low at 06:40 (0.3 m). Waders everywhere on the exposed mud: Common Redshank, Common Greenshank, a dozen Marsh Sandpipers. Scanned from the bund with binoculars.
Sunset from the sea-facing bastion. Black Kites circled over the fishing village and a Peregrine Falcon shot past once, possibly, too fast to be sure. Mosquitoes came out right after dusk.
Asian Koel calling from the neighbour's mango tree since 05:30, relentless. Purple Sunbird male on the hibiscus pot in the morning sun.
Egrets on the mudflats at falling tide, around fifteen Little Egrets and three Great Egrets. A Black-headed Ibis flew over the mangroves. Smell of the creek strong in the heat.
Smoggy, grey evening; US AQI 152 and you couldn't see the horizon. Only a few gulls about. Cut the walk short because my throat was scratchy.
Oriental Magpie Robin singing from the lamp post, a full rich song. Ashy Prinia and a Common Tailorbird in the hedges near the gate. Pleasant, 27°C, light wind.
Thunderstorm rolled in from the sea at 16:00, lightning over the salt pans. Left before the rain hit; the egrets all lifted at once with the first thunder.
Greater Coucal walking through the dry grass along the moat, deep hooting call. A troop of macaques on the ramparts made everyone nervous.
Clear night after a windy day. Spotted an owl shape on the mobile tower, probably a Barn Owl from the pale underside, possibly. Stars visible for once.
Western Reef Herons, both grey and white forms, fishing in the rock pools at low tide. Crabs scattering everywhere. Sand firm near the high-water line.
Little Grebe diving in the lake, two adults and a striped juvenile. Lake level still high from the monsoon; the lower path was waterlogged.
Brahminy Kite hunting low over the creek, picked something off the water surface. White-throated Kingfisher calling from the electric wire. Muggy, apparent 34°C.
Early morning at the fort with fog lifting off the ruins, very atmospheric. Golden Oriole whistled from the tamarind, first one this season. Black Drongos on the ramparts.
Dust haze all afternoon, US AQI 135. Black Kites soaring in the thermals, maybe thirty of them over the market. Kept the windows shut.
Huge waves after the depression offshore; red flag at the lifeguard hut. Terns, probably Gull-billed Terns, fishing beyond the breakers. Stayed well back from the water.
Rose-ringed Parakeets squabbling over nest holes in the dead palm. A Shikra flew through and silenced everything for a minute.
Quiet visit, nothing identified. High tide covered all the mud and the heat was heavy, 35°C.
Visited after the evening drizzle; the stone was steaming. Purple-rumped Sunbirds in the flowering creeper by the chapel. Spotted Owlets started calling at dusk.
First cool morning, 23°C at 06:30 and a light northerly breeze. Red-vented Bulbuls bathing in the water dish, three of them taking turns.
Kentish Plovers on the upper beach, maybe eight, very well camouflaged against the sand. Falling tide, calm sea, golden light around 17:45.
Western Marsh Harrier quartering over the salt pans, first harrier of the winter. Ducks? Not sure, too far. Low tide at 10:10.
Moorhen and a Purple Swamphen in the reeds at the far corner of the lake. Rain all morning, umbrella walk, very few people.
White-throated Kingfisher on the fort moat, loud laughing call. Indian Pond Heron in the moat water too. Warm, humid, AQI 88.
Sunset walk; the sky went pink then purple. Gulls roosting on the sandbar offshore. Wind died down completely after dark and we headed home.
Collared Kingfisher in the mangroves, fairly confident, blue-and-white with that broad collar. Rising tide flooded the channel quickly. Mosquitoes bad near the mangroves.
Fireworks practice somewhere nearby rattled the pigeons off the ledges. Smoke haze and US AQI 160 by 21:00.
Black-rumped Flameback drumming on the old rain tree. Leaves still dripping from overnight rain; the air smelled of wet earth.
Long walk through the fort's inner courtyard. Common Hoopoe probing in the lawn by the ticket counter, crest fanned. Bright, sunny, 31°C.
Morning low tide at 08:15. Terek Sandpipers, three of them, running fast at the water edge; possibly a Broad-billed Sandpiper too. Hazy sun.
Jellyfish washed up along the tideline after the storm surge. Few birds; a Brahminy Kite overhead. Walked only on the firm sand.
Rain again in the afternoon, a short cloudburst. A wet Common Myna sat hunched on the dish antenna. Rooftop puddles everywhere.
Spotted Dove cooing from the bandstand roof. Plum-headed Parakeet? Possibly, heard only. Pleasant evening, 26°C.
Crested Serpent Eagle calling high above the fort, circling on flat wings. Hot midday, 34°C. Saw it from the shade of the arch.
Tide very high at 13:00, over 4 m. Water reached the bund steps. Little Cormorants drying their wings on the stakes in the creek.
Early morning, mist over the sea and the sand still damp. Sanderlings, a small flock of about twelve, chasing each wave in and out.
Rufous Treepie raided the neighbour's balcony for food scraps. Clear blue sky, AQI 54, best air of the month.
Asian Paradise Flycatcher, a white male with long tail streamers, in the bamboo clump. Confident. Overcast and breezy.
Four Painted Storks feeding in the shallow pools as the tide fell around 15:30. Pinkish wing feathers glowing in the low sun.
Night visit to the fort for the full moon. Indian Scops Owl calling, possibly, a soft 'wut' from the trees. Bats everywhere around the towers.
Strong onshore wind, 9 m/s, sand stinging the legs. Gulls hanging in the wind over the dunes. Short visit.
Blyth's Reed Warbler tacking in the potted bougainvillea, a winter visitor back. Cool evening, 25°C.
Osprey perched on the high-tension pylon over the creek with a fish. Confident. Calm water, slack tide.
Kids feeding the ducks at the lake. Spot-billed Ducks, five, plus the resident Little Grebes. Warm afternoon.
Drizzle stopped by 17:00 and a rainbow appeared over the fort walls. Ashy Drongo, fairly confident, on the dead branch by the well.
Low tide at 07:30 exposed a huge sandbar. Greater Sand Plovers and Lesser Sand Plovers mixed, plus three Eurasian Curlews. Stayed on the firm sand above the waterline.
Hazy and smoky over the creek, US AQI 145, the far bank barely visible. A few Little Egrets and a lone Grey Heron. Short visit.
Diwali night: fireworks until midnight, no birds. AQI over 200 the next morning.
Morning after Diwali, the park quiet and smoky. Even the Common Mynas were subdued. AQI 190.
Peafowl, a male in full plumage, crossing the dirt track behind the fort. Cool morning, 22°C, clear.
Last visit of October: falling tide at 17:05, the mud lit gold. Common Kingfisher confident, perched on the mangrove root. Little Egrets and a Western Reef Heron working the channel.
